quotes.note: Sustained external scene narration follows Denny and Mitch as 'they,' with no participating narrator framing the passage.
The isolated sentence contains no narrator reference and cannot establish person.
A standalone location phrase lacks enough narrative context to identify a voice.
Gnomic commentary, apparently within quoted speech, does not identify the base narrator.
After an explicit Chapter 100 boundary, Alex narrates as 'I' and 'our'; the preceding sustained Denny passage is third-person base narration and independently reveals the book's mixed structure.
Outside the direct speech, the beats 'I said' and 'She laughed and reached up to kiss me' expose a participating first-person narrator.

person_note: Cross Fire sustains two base modes: Alex Cross narrates his chapters in first person, while Denny, Mitch, Kyle Craig, and other antagonist material is narrated in third person. The Goodreads evidence captures both modes—including an interior transition at Chapter 100—and the credited opening excerpt independently alternates them across chapters. Dialogue and gnomic fragments were not promoted to base narration. No credible contrary structure was found.
